items.title: Add slide-repair-coupling-across-pipe-joint task
items.body:
Adds `tasks/slide-repair-coupling-across-pipe-joint`: a 1 1/2-inch PVC drain line under repair. A new length of pipe has its far end pushed home in a fixed elbow; its near end rests on a block, sagging 1.5 cm below the end of the installed pipe it has to join. A slip coupling (a repair sleeve with no stop inside) sits on the installed pipe. The task is to close the joint the way a plumber does: lift the new pipe's loose end into line with the installed pipe, slide the coupling along the installed pipe across the joint until it is centred, and let go, so that the coupling holds the new pipe in line.

The new pipe pivots in the elbow and cannot slide along its length (it already reaches the installed pipe), so the coupling cannot be put on it first and pushed on end-first; while the pipe sags, the coupling's mouth meets its end face instead of passing over it. One arm has to hold the new pipe in line while the other slides the coupling. With the left arm kept still (`PIPE_ONE_ARM=1`), the same push stops against the end of the sagging pipe and the run scores 0.

The scripted demo closes the left gripper on the new pipe 10 cm from its far end and lifts it into line (the pipe turns about the elbow's socket); the right gripper comes down behind the coupling with its fingers astride the installed pipe and pushes the coupling's end along it, across the joint, until each pipe is 34 mm inside it. The right gripper backs off, the left lets go, and the coupling keeps the new pipe in line. The pipes, the elbow (a socket with 1.2 mm of play) and the coupling (a 16-sided bore with chamfered mouths) are rigid bodies built from several shapes by `bodykit.py`, next to the task file: importing it hooks `yam_arena.scene` when the simulator starts (without changing yam_arena) and reports each body's pose to the scoring.

- Category: Impact on jobs
- Scores: Dream-1 run 0.0; scripted demo 1.0 (partial credit, the best stage reached: 0.25 the new pipe's near end held in line; 0.5 the coupling across the joint, each pipe at least 10 mm inside it; 0.75 the coupling centred, each pipe at least 30 mm inside it; pulling the new pipe out of the elbow, or a pipe or the coupling falling onto the table, sets 0 for the rest of the run)
- Run limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz)

items.title: Fit the Right Bit and Secure a Loose Drawer Handle
items.body:
Adds a tabletop furniture-maintenance task: inspect a loose drawer-handle screw, choose a compatible tip, physically fit it to an empty powered screwdriver, tighten the handle while steadying the drawer, and leave the stopped tool released in its stand.

Tip compatibility is determined by geometry. The socket transmits torque through contact, and passive grip/pressure switches enable the motor. Scoring measures handle closure and the released tool's final rest state; the ideal screw-to-carriage coupling and other physical simplifications are documented.

Validation: complete final-layout scripted demo scores 1.0 in 3,797 of 4,800 steps. The initial idle state scores 0; a separate wrong-installed-hex-tip diagnostic scores 0. Dream-1 beta completed one uninterrupted 4,800-step simulation trial with score 0.0 and zero errored trials.

Media: M-PY8PDZ.

items.title: Seat a keyed coupling and prove drive transfer
items.body:
Robot drive maintenance requires a coupling to transmit rotation after assembly. This task checks both seating over unequal drive dogs and actual motion of the lower rotor. Placing the coupling on top without transferring rotation cannot earn full credit.

Engagement must remain continuous during drive transfer. A physics contact monitor rejects direct robot drive on the lower rotor.

Dream 1 scored 0.0 in a complete 2400 step trial. The separate scripted demo scored 1.0 in 462 steps. Both use seed 0 with no object jitter and the exact same task source. The selected model trial kept one continuous session and had no runtime errors. Earlier capacity and session expiry failures are excluded from the reported score.

The uploaded videos are native 1280 by 720 H264. Every selected model camera contains 2401 frames. The folder includes numerical scoring and complete setup dimensions and reproduction commands and source hashes and a measured score plot.

This keeps the original task idea from PR #192 and replaces its withdrawn pending snapshot with corrected scoring and genuine model evidence.

items.title: Seat a keyed coupling and prove drive transfer
items.body:
This task seats an upper coupling over unequal drive dogs then turns the lower rotor through the coupling. Full credit requires measured drive transfer and stable seating after both grippers release.

The scripted demonstration reaches 1.0 within 600 control steps. An exact repeat also reaches 1.0. Seating requires relative alignment within 5 degrees. Both uploaded videos contain the same scripted demonstration with synchronized top and wrist views at native 720p. No model execution or model score is claimed. The package includes every solid and joint plus numerical scoring and reproduction commands.

items.title: Replace a cut-out drain-pipe section with slip couplings
items.body:
This task tests a dry-fit drain-pipe repair. The robot must fit a loose replacement section into a cut-out gap in a fixed pipe run and join both ends with closed slip couplings. A closed coupling can't get onto the run once both ends are captured, so the matching couplings have to be staged on the old pipe ends (or on the new section) before the gap closes and then slid back over each joint. Two look-alike couplings of the wrong size must be left aside. It is a common plumbing and maintenance job (O*NET 47-2152, 49-9071) that combines sequencing, size discrimination and coaxial sliding with two arms.

- `task.json`: instruction, setup, tiered scoring (0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0, with a sticky zero for parts falling off the bench), run limit and fidelity notes
- `README.md`: parts and layout, how the simulator builds them, scoring details, the open-loop demo plan, and the commands to run and score a trial
- `repair_drain_pipe_with_slip_couplings.py`: scene, scorer (release and 1 s stillness for full score) and scripted demo
- `test_repair_drain_pipe_with_slip_couplings.py`: layout and scorer tests, including partial, decoy and cheat layouts, plus demo reach and run-limit checks
- `yam_parts.py`, `yam_joints.py`: primitive part kit used by the scene

Take a spring-loaded bayonet coupling sleeve off its shaft: push down, turn, lift, turn back, pull off
items.body:
Adds a bimanual task: take a spring-loaded bayonet coupling sleeve off its shaft. The track inside the sleeve is hidden and has two stages (push down, turn, lift, turn back, pull off); a straight pull or a single turn stops at a ledge. The loose sleeve then goes in a tray.

The task runs through Isaac Lab-Arena and Inspect Robots. Dream-1 run: 0.0 (6,000 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 (1,490 steps).

This replaces an earlier submission of the same task that was withdrawn to correct its text; the scene, scorer, runs and media are unchanged.

items.title: Remove a multistage bayonet sleeve
items.body:
Adds a custom unpowered two-pin coupling fixture: release a captive sleeve through a spring-loaded multilevel internal track and rotational reversal, then leave it resting in a parts tray. Physical contacts constrain the release; the numeric scorer awards 0.5 for a released, stationary sleeve and 1.0 after 20 seconds hands off.

Validated on the YAM/Arena Brev environment: Dream-1 scored 0.0 after the full 6,000-action budget in one continuous session; the saved robot-action demonstration scored 1.0 after 1,490 actions with a 26.85-second final hold. Actual model/demo H.264 videos and the reset screenshot are linked by media ID M-Y682WB. Package integrity, source binding, complete video decoding and one-task scope checks passed.

The README records setup, runtime, reproduction, scoring, scoped measurement evidence, rigid-contact limitations and the earlier provider timeout that produced no score. All task semantics are preserved after publication metadata and whitespace-only packaging changes.
